title: Dispatch BBA 9: Archive Preserves Names of the St Oran Patients
summary: The bell is silent, but the city has amended the account of its oldest hospital fire.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The municipal archive has added Elsie Gray's name to the St. Oran's register without removing the original forty-one entries. The new page is dated June 21, 1882, and includes a note stating that the record was corrected by the Eidetical Institute with the cooperation of the surviving family.

The sixty-three living witnesses have been examined by the Institute. None has reported further calls, sounds, or apparitions. Their names remain in the municipal record as persons who were briefly entered in a hospital register that should have closed in 1874.

Mrs. Arden visited the site with her grandmother's photograph. She had wondered for years why Elsie never spoke of the fire. "She remembered the nurse who sent her home," Mrs. Arden said. "She thought the nurse had died because of her. She was waiting to be forgiven by the record."

Inspector Voss has asked the city to place a small marker at the east edge of the square for the patients who died in the fire. The council has agreed, with the inscription to be chosen by Miss Morrow and the archive together.

At dawn, our reporter stood with the porter beneath the market arch. Six carts passed, the clock struck six, and no other sound rose from the ground. The square has returned to ordinary use. The case is filed under Field Reports until further notice.
